WELCOME TO LIFT LAB

Make the elevator behave.

Choose a floor, run the elevator, and adjust the gains while it moves. Your goal: a quick arrival without bouncing or hurting the passengers.

  1. Start with P. It pushes toward the target. Too much makes the car oscillate.
  2. Add D. It brakes based on velocity, reducing overshoot.
  3. Add a little I. It accumulates error. This balanced system needs no I to hold height; try it to see how stored error can add overshoot.

Integral accumulation max limits the stored integral of position error to ± the value you choose (in meter-seconds). The I force is Ki × 1000 × this accumulated value. Reducing the limit clamps the stored value immediately; zero disables accumulation. The limit is retained on Reset and when selecting presets.

Zero I on error sign change clears the integral when the error switches between positive and negative, including after changing the target. It is off by default. Enabling it does not clear the integral immediately. It discards stored control effort and can change the settling behavior.

Try Challenges for three guided experiments. Reset starts a fresh ride with your current gains. Clean cabin removes stains without changing the simulation.

What is being simulated?

800 kg cabin + 75 kg per passenger; 9.81 m/s² gravity; 1000 N·s/m passive drive damping; ±24 kN motor limit. An ideal adjustable counterweight always equals cabin plus passenger mass. With a 1:1 rope, acceleration is (motor force − drag) / (cabin mass + counterweight mass). The damping force is −1000 × velocity (N), independent of the PID gains. It dissipates motion like drive/guide resistance and vanishes at rest. Gravity cancels between the two sides; the motor has no gravity feedforward. A stopped cabin holds height at zero motor force. A moving cabin retains inertia until braking and drag stop it. Passenger motion is a visual approximation; the main model treats passengers as part of the cabin mass. Displayed gains are in thousands of SI units. D uses measured velocity, avoiding setpoint kick. Conditional integration limits windup. The passenger animation and injuries are stylized gameplay, not a human safety model.

Settling requires error below 0.10 m and speed below 0.08 m/s for one second. Overshoot is measured relative to the distance of the latest commanded trip. Peak g shows cabin acceleration, excluding normal gravity.
